Subject: Re: sudden 503s from archer4b (started 09:05) — triage update

TL;DR: root cause appears to be a KV cache eviction edge-case in the quantized execution path for archer4b. We have a safe mitigation path and are rolling it out now (routing + config toggle).

Details:
- Symptoms: elevated 5xx/503 surface across requests with longer prefix histories; CPU/GPU utilization on the hosting nodes was normal. Correlation between failures and requests hitting quantized execution with large KV lookups.
- Root cause hypothesis: an off-by-one eviction during KV cache refill in the quantized kernel path leads to invalid pointer dereference under concurrent prefix refresh. This triggers a generation failure (503) rather than a graceful fallback.

Mitigation rolled out (09:40 PDT):
1) Router rule: divert 20% -> archer4b-v2 (non-quantized) in the same region.
2) Toggle: temporarily disable the new quantized kernel for archer4b on the affected pool.
3) Cache: enable conservative prefix cache retention for critical customer routes (including DataForge).

We've attached a telemetry snapshot. We'll monitor error rate for the next 30 minutes and expand rollback if it's holding. If this stabilizes, we'll schedule a follow-up patch release to fix the eviction bug and re-enable the quantized kernel after validation.

Attachment: archer4b-telemetry-snapshot-0918.json (sandboxed telemetry subset).

-Karthik
Staff SW Eng, Serving Runtime

Subject: Archer4b 503 wave — customer update and next steps

Hi Emily — quick update from the team: we identified a quantized KV-cache eviction bug affecting archer4b that manifested under specific prefix patterns. We pushed an immediate mitigation (routing to archer4b-v2 + disabling the quantized kernel for the affected fleet) at ~09:40 PDT.

What we saw: error rate for your sampled traffic dropped from ~18% -> ~1.2% within 10 minutes of the mitigation. We're continuing to monitor for regressions over the next 2 hours.

What we will do next:
- Engineering will ship a patch to fix the eviction edge-case; target for canary release is EOD tomorrow (08/16).
- We'll coordinate a controlled re-enable of the quantized kernel behind a canary and automated health checks.
- If you prefer, we can keep you on the safer variant (archer4b-v2) for 48 hours while we validate.

Credits / compensation: given the scope and customer impact, I'm opening a support credit request with finance. We'll follow up with a formal credit amount and how it will be applied to your invoice.

Would you be willing to run a 15-minute smoke test at ~10:15 PDT to confirm the drop in your environment? If that works, we can close this as recovered and share postmortem notes.

Apologies again for the disruption and thanks for the quick alert — that helped us isolate the failure vector faster.

Best,
